source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Without names, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with names, it is the mother of the ten thousand things.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical path along which people travel or something proceeds.
Sentence Translations (English): The road is difficult and long.
The gentleman's way is practiced throughout the realm.
This route reaches the commanderies and kingdoms.
There is a path in the mountains that can be traveled.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To put an idea or matter into words.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This verbal use concerns articulating something, not the philosophical Way.
Sentence Translations (English): He stated what he had seen.
The minister explained its cause.
The historian recounted past events.
The father recited ancient teachings.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The underlying course or principle through which reality operates and by which things arise.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this line, it denotes the ultimate Way, distinguished from any Way that can be fully expressed.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that an action is allowed or authorized.
Sentence Translations (English): You may enter.
This saying must not be forgotten.
If a gentleman may serve, then he serves.
The people may be moved to the south.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses approval that something meets a desired standard.
Sentence Translations (English): This plan is usable.
His writing is worth viewing.
This child can be taught.
This person is worth speaking with.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Is capable of being expressed or explained in words.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It marks possibility, specifically the possibility of verbal articulation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To judge someone or something negatively and fault it.
Sentence Translations (English): It was not what he did.
Everyone criticized him.
I dare not criticize the former kings.
It is not another person's fault.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates the following statement or identifies it as false or different from what is asserted.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it denies that the expressible Way is the constant Way.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A way or principle that is not permanently or universally constant.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The phrase contrasts with the ultimate Way by stressing its lack of permanence or absoluteness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The public esteem or renown attached to a person.
Sentence Translations (English): His reputation was established throughout the realm.
Gain and harm are insufficient to move his reputation.
The gentleman dislikes dying with his name unrecognized.
His fame was heard among the feudal lords.
Sentences: 君子疾沒世而名不稱焉。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To assign or use a designation for someone or something.
Sentence Translations (English): He named it Uncarved Simplicity.
The historian named that mountain.
The father named his son.
It cannot be named.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A word or designation used to identify and distinguish a person, thing, or concept.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this parallel clause, naming is treated as verbal designation rather than reputation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A designation that is not permanently or universally fixed.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It contrasts with an ultimate, constant designation that could permanently capture reality.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To be without something that could otherwise be possessed or present.
Sentence Translations (English): The state has no weapons or warfare.
The household has no surplus wealth.
The people show no signs of hunger.
The room has no unnecessary possessions.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The absence or nonexistence of something, here absence of a name or designation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Placed before 名, it means namelessness rather than simple refusal or prohibition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; philosophical literary register

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The cosmic totality of Heaven and Earth, understood as the encompassing natural world.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The paired expression denotes the cosmos as a whole, not merely the sky and ground as physical surfaces.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; cosmological literary register

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person object pronoun referring to a previously mentioned person or thing.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): As a pronoun, it occupies an object position rather than linking two noun phrases.
Sentence Translations (English): Study it and practice it regularly.
The people love him.
The king summoned him.
One who knows it is not as good as one who delights in it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A relational particle linking a noun phrase to the noun that follows it, here marking the beginning belonging to Heaven and Earth.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It forms a possessive or attributive relationship rather than an independent lexical meaning.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical literary register in the received Laozi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To start an action, process, or undertaking.
Sentence Translations (English): In spring life begins to grow.
The king began governing the state.
The student began with investigating things.
The rain began to fall.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks the earliest stage or first occurrence in a sequence.
Sentence Translations (English): At first I did not know.
At first it is difficult, but in the end it is easy.
At first he treated him well, but later he doubted him.
At first he learned the true circumstances.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The initial point from which something starts or comes into existence.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to the origin of Heaven and Earth before differentiated things are named.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension; cosmological literary register
